stories.headline: Intelligence chief reportedly named AI czar
stories.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that DNI Jay Clayton will lead a White House AI task force and deliver recommendations within 120 days. The panel will review AI risks, incident reporting and federal response capabilities.

stories.headline: OpenAI safety employee resigns with warning
stories.summary: Former safety employee David Robinson said OpenAI's rapid-release culture creates unacceptable risk. OpenAI says it holds back models when necessary and works to keep capabilities within safe limits.

stories.headline: Supreme Court opens with major climate case
stories.summary: Exxon and Suncor seek dismissal of Boulder's climate-damages lawsuit, arguing federal law precludes its state claims. The ruling could affect roughly 60 similar cases; Justice Samuel Alito recused himself.

stories.headline: Brazil votes in closely divided election
stories.summary: President Lula and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro lead a polarized first-round vote shaped by corruption allegations and economic anxiety. Polls show a likely October 25 runoff, with neither side assured victory.

stories.headline: Germany expands Ukraine aid as Kyiv is attacked
stories.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz arrived in Kyiv amid air alerts and explosions. Germany plans €1 billion in military aid, €350 million for energy repairs and a drone-production agreement as Russian strikes intensify.
